what: PLAN-POLICE-VOICE-KAZE-DETAIL Step K1: Kaze FR's proportions, stations, fender peaks and wheel track
machine: the user's Windows 11 PC, Chrome (Claude in Chrome), npm run dev:local
how: The exact production path (buildVehicleShape, createVehicleAsset from src/traffic/vehicle-shape.mjs and src/player/vehicle-asset.mjs, unmodified) was imported into a same-origin dev-server page and rendered/queried directly. qa/gta-upgrade/carbench.html itself 404s under this session's dev server (every path under /qa/ does, including the pre-existing punchbench.html and vehiclebench.html -- a routing limitation of this dev-server session, not something this step introduced), so it was not opened as a real page load this session.

front_overhang.note: plan says 'about 0.85 m'; the loft's axle is symmetric front/rear, so hitting the wheelbase exactly trades off against the overhang

fender_peak.method: buildVehicleShape('ownCar').geometry.paint vertex Y at the front axle Z: centreline (x~0) vs fender edge (|x|>width*.35)
fender_peak.note: confirmed by tests/kaze-detail.test.mjs; also confirmed opt-in only -- the sedan silhouette keeps an exactly flat bonnet at the same query

wheel_arch_exposure.method: min body-paint vertex Y at the front axle Z among outer-flank points (excludes the floor and its rounded corner), divided by wheel diameter

wheel_track_fix.problem: the shared wheel-anchor formula (W/2 - wheelWidth*.80) tucks a wheel in 80% of its own width from the outer skin; on Kaze FR's low body this buries most of the wheel behind the arch wall (visually confirmed, see before-track-fix-grid.jpg)
wheel_track_fix.fix: a new per-type VEHICLES.ownCar.track = .55 (default .80, unused by any other type) moves the wheel centre from x=0.716 to x=0.767
wheel_track_fix.honest_visual_note: a second render after the fix (side-front3q-after-track-fix.jpg) still reads the wheel as mostly hidden from a straight side angle -- the 60%-of-height exposure the geometry test confirms is real (verified three ways: the test, a direct vertex query, and hand computation), but it is the LOWER 63% of a circle bounded by a horizontal sill line, which is a narrower-looking crescent than 63% of a rectangle would be, and the track move (5 cm) is small next to the car's ~2 m width. The renderer was also visibly unstable this session (see below), so a cleaner, larger, better-lit carbench capture is worth the user's own eyes before deciding whether the track number needs to move further.

renderer_stability: Chrome automation hit repeated 'renderer may be frozen or unresponsive' / 45s timeouts this session, consistent with the ~2 GB free of 16 GB already noted in evidence/police-voice-kaze/step-p/metrics.json. Several capture attempts had to be abandoned or retried in a fresh tab.
